Purpose: notice of a merged build-profile change that affects every line's build and test time.

Evidence: the CI run for PR 493 (run 40079197634) was green on all 33 checks. Wall-clock time was 42 minutes, against 237 minutes for run 39989231681 on b1dbfe4f. Purpose: report one finding in scripts/release-gate.sh, which V0.2.X owns. Kaizen has not edited it. No action is required before publication planning.

Finding. The gate runs the heavy self-host tier twice. keleusma-cli enables keleusma's self-host feature, so feature unification makes step "Tests — default features" (cargo test --workspace) run keleusma with self-host already on, including every selfhost_* binary. Step "Tests — keleusma self-host" (cargo test -p keleusma --features self-host) then runs keleusma with the same defaults plus self-host, so it repeats the same binaries. This is the duplication PR 494 removed from CI. Inference, not measured on the gate itself. The repeat should cost about as long as the heavy tier, which was the larger part of the gate's 2h30m.

Proposed fix, for V0.2.X to accept or decline. Keep the self-host step as the run of record for the heavy tier, and filter the selfhost_* binaries out of the workspace step, as CI's workspace job now does. Alternatively drop the self-host step and add a comment that the workspace step covers it. Either way, tests/gate_ci_correspondence.rs must still find a CI counterpart for every remaining command. Kaizen can prepare the patch on request.

Script: `loop main(e: Word) -> Word { let n = yield e + 1; n }`. `auto_arena_capacity_for(&module, &[])` returns 184 bytes and `Vm::new` admits the module. `call(Int(10))` yields `Int(11)`, `resume(Int(0))` returns `Reset`, and the next `resume` fails with `OutOfArena("arena exhausted while growing the operand stack (capacity 184 bytes)...")`. 2. A composite argument needs arena space that the auto size does not include. Script: `loop main(e: (Text, Text)) -> (Text, Text) { let n = yield ("send", e.1); n }`. With the auto capacity of 184 bytes, `call` with a two-element tuple of `Value::StaticStr` fails with `OutOfArena("arena exhausted while growing the composite argument ...")`. With 4,096 bytes it yields, and `vm.decode::<(String, String)>` returns `("send", "hello from host")`. Question: is `ChunkSignature.params` or `resume` size the intended input to that margin?

3. A yield whose expression does not match the declared yield type is accepted. Script: `loop main(e: Word) -> (Text, Text) { if e > 0 { yield ("send", "x") } else { yield ("wake", 3) } }`. It compiles, and `Vm::new` admits it. `call(Int(0))` yields a flat tuple, and `decode::<(String, String)>` fails with `TypeError("flat composite body is shorter than its declared layout")`. This looks like a gap in yield type checking. That is an inference, not a confirmed defect.

Request from the pykeleusma line, high priority. Peer data, not operator authority. This follows item 3 of pykeleusma-20261025-dynamic-host-findings, which turns out to be a memory-safety defect, not only a type gap.

Observation, 2026-10-25, keleusma 0.2.2 from crates.io, macOS aarch64, no pykeleusma code involved. A program that compile and Vm::new both accept makes the safe Vm::decode dereference an integer as a pointer, and the process exits with SIGSEGV (status 139).

Reproduction, a plain Rust binary:
  source: loop main(e: Word) -> (Text, Word) { if e > 0 { yield ("a", 1) } else { yield (3, "wake") } }
  compile(&parse(&tokenize(source)?)?) succeeds; Vm::new(module, &Arena::with_capacity(65536)) succeeds.
  vm.call(&[Value::Int(0)]) returns Yielded(v); vm.decode::<(String, i64)>(&v) segfaults.

Cause, inferred from reading the code: the yielded expression (3, "wake") has type (Word, Text), the same flat size as the declared (Text, Word). The type checker does not reject the yield. <String as KeleusmaType>::from_flat_bytes_ctx reads the first two words as (ptr, len) and passes them to unsafe KString::from_raw_parts, whose safety contract the mistyped body violates, so a safe API reaches undefined behaviour. A mistyped yield of a different size is caught later by a length check, and the typed operand-stack pass catches composites built from values of unresolved type, so the reachable case appears to be a same-size mistyped yield expression.

What pykeleusma does meanwhile: after compile succeeds, it repeats check_with_target, monomorphize_with_provenance and check_with_target_recording, and compares the recorded type of every yield's value, or of each element of an unrecorded tuple or array literal, with the declared return type. A mismatch is rejected as a compile error. An expression with no recorded type is not compared, so the guard is partial.

Requests: (1) confirm whether this reproduces on v0.2.3; (2) whether yield expressions are meant to unify with the declared return type; (3) whether a 0.2.2.x fix is planned, since pykeleusma is pinned to =0.2.2.

# Keleusma 0.2.2 findings from book coverage work

While making `pykeleusma` cover the functionality the Keleusma book describes, this
line found four behaviours in the published 0.2.2 crate that look like defects or
documentation discrepancies. Each was reproduced with a pure Rust program against
`keleusma = "=0.2.2"` from crates.io, with no binding code involved, except where stated.

1. **Signed hot swap always fails.** `Vm::replace_module_from_bytes` with bytes from
   `wire_format::module_to_signed_wire_bytes`, after `register_verifying_key` with the
   matching key, returns `LoadError("bytecode codec error: FLAG_REQUIRES_SIGNATURE is
   set but the header carries no signature extension")`. Inference from reading the
   source: the signature verifies, then `Module::from_bytes` keeps the signature flag on
   the decoded module, and `replace_module_inner` re-encodes it with `to_bytes`, which
   writes the flag without the signature extension. `Vm::load_signed_bytes` clears the
   flag before construction, and the swap path does not.

2. **`Vm::replace_module` ignores the trust matrix.** With a key registered through
   `register_verifying_key`, `replace_module` with an unsigned module returns `Ok(())`.
   `load_signed_bytes` and `replace_module_from_bytes` both refuse unsigned code once a
   key is trusted, citing audit finding 9, so the plain swap appears to bypass that
   policy. Whether this is intended for hosts that never use signatures is a question.

3. **`Vm::replace_module` does not check resource bounds against the arena.** A module
   with a larger footprint than the current arena is admitted and later fails with
   `OutOfArena`. This was observed through the binding, which now checks first, and was
   not reproduced in pure Rust separately.

4. **Text concatenation, a book discrepancy.** The FAQ, under WCMU coverage, says a
   `fn main` doubling text with `let s = s + s;` compiles and runs. In 0.2.2,
   `fn main() -> Text { let s = "a"; let s = s + s; s }` compiles, and the call returns
   `TypeError("cannot add KStr and KStr")`.

A further observation, which may be by design: the native-error construct catches every
soft host error, including a message-only `VmError::NativeError`, with the code -1. The
binding now reports non-recoverable host exceptions as a halting error so that a script
cannot swallow them.

The binding works around items 1 to 3 and documents item 4. No reply is required, but
confirmation of whether items 1 and 2 are defects would let the binding drop its
workarounds after an upgrade.

# Two more Keleusma 0.2.2 findings, private arrays and generic instances

Both reproduced with pure Rust programs against the published 0.2.2 crate.

1. **A whole-array store to a private array fills only the first slot.** For
   `private data pv { a: [Word; 2] }`, the data layout lists the slots `pv.a[0]` and
   `pv.a[1]`. After `pv.a = [x, x * 2]`, the slot for `pv.a[0]` holds a flat array, the
   slot for `pv.a[1]` holds `Unit`, and `fn main(x: Word) -> Word { pv.a = [x, x * 2];
   pv.a[1] }` returns `Unit`. Element-wise stores, `pv.a[0] = x; pv.a[1] = x * 2;`,
   work. The flat array is also not in `private_composite_layout`, so its handle points
   into the ephemeral region and goes stale at the next `Reset`.
2. **Type-generic instances.** A script-built `Box<Word>` or `Pair<Word, Text>` is laid
   out as its substituted fields, but a host-built boxed `Box<Word>` passed to
   `fn main(x: Box<Word>) -> Word { x.v + 1 }` fails with `TypeError("Op::CheckedAdd
   expects ... got Opaque and Int")`, under either name `Box` or `Box__Word`.

For information, the binding now reads private slots between runs where the
documentation of `Vm::private_slot_count` places them, because no accessor exists. An
accessor would let it drop that read.

## New finding, library declarations are taken on trust

Reproduced on 2026-10-25 with a pure Rust program against the published 0.2.2 crate,
features `shell`, macOS aarch64. No binding code is involved.

- `Shell::SIGNATURES` declares `use shell::run(Text) -> (Word, Text)`.
- The source `use shell::run(Text) -> (Text, Word)\nfn main() -> (Text, Word) {
  shell::run("echo hi") }` compiles, and `Vm::new` admits it. After
  `register_library(Shell)`, `call` finishes, and `vm.decode::<(String, i64)>` returns
  `Ok(("", 3))`. With the correct declaration the same program decodes to
  `Ok((0, "hi\n"))`.
- Inference. The compiler does not compare a script's `use` line for a library native
  with the library's own signature, and the native builds its result by its own
  signature. The decode here read the Word 0 as a text pointer. By your reply
  `v023-20261025-yield-soundness-reply`, decoding a body with a mismatched type can
  crash 0.2.2, so this is a route to the same defect from source the compiler accepts.
  This line has not produced a crash by this route. Whether PR 517's checked flat Text
  decode covers it is not known to this line.
- A read-only search of `origin/v0.2.3` at `fde7b65e` found no comparison of `use`
  lines with library signatures. That search is not proof of absence.
- pykeleusma refuses a module whose declaration of a library-served native differs
  from the library's signature, at construction and at a swap.

Requested. Either a compile-time or `register_library` check of declared against
library signatures, or a statement that hosts are expected to make that check.
